notes:
Seven bullets, one action. Bullet 2 IS the mission -- the cutscene ends with the next mission ('Back to the Beginning') already active -- so bullets 3, 4 and 6 are consequences (what happens if you warp out before unlocking anything, what the maws do from now on, why a present-day maw is unresponsive) and none of them is a rung. Bullet 5, 'travel to the other two Shadowreign Cavernous Maws to unlock them', happens AFTER the handoff to the next mission and is travel plumbing, not this mission's work, so it is not a step either.

GIVER: AGREES with chronicle. The header offers three maws -- Batallia Downs, Rolanberry Fields, Sauromugue Champaign -- and a player clicks exactly one, which is an OR no ordered ladder expresses; I took Batallia Downs because chronicle_snpc already reads 'cavernous maw in batallia downs', so the marker does not move. Writing the other two as a group would assert you must visit all three, which is false, so the alternatives live in the step note instead. 'Cavernous Maw' probes clean (keys ['cavernous maw'], not ambiguous), so this is a real marker and not a name that matches the world.

Bullet 1 ('Visit any Cavernous Maw in the following locations:') lists nothing -- its location table did not survive the prepass -- which is why the three zones here come from the Start field. No grid for any maw appears anywhere on the page, so grid is null rather than guessed. The Pure white feather is the header's Reward, so by hard rule 7 it is not evidence: it proves the mission is over, not that the click happened. Note also that the page is tagged Category:Disambiguation; the sibling article 'Cavernous Maws' (the location list) is a different page and was not read.

start.raw: Cavernous Maw in Batallia Downs, Rolanberry Fields, or Sauromugue Champaign.

steps.note: ANY one of three maws does: Batallia Downs, Rolanberry Fields or Sauromugue Champaign. Batallia Downs is recorded because that is the maw the shipped index already points at. You are dropped into one of the three Shadowreign zones at random regardless of which you used, and if you warp out before unlocking anything you must return to the maw in the zone you landed in.

notes:
This mission is a container for a THREE-WAY NATIONAL BRANCH and only its last line is a step. Bullet 1 is cross-storyline advice (you may run Rhapsodies 2-16 alongside it). Bullet 2 says the mission triggers itself off the previous BCNM cutscene and then lists six quests in three pairs -- Bastok: Storm on the Horizon, Fire in the Hole; San d'Oria: Perils of the Griffon, In a Haze of Glory; Windurst: When One Man Is Not Enough, A Feast for Gnats -- of which a player does exactly the two for their own allegiance. Bullet 3 is the only instruction: after those, examine the Lion Springs Tavern door in Southern San d'Oria (S) at (K-6).

I did NOT put those six quests in gates.prev. prev is an AND-list and four of the six are quests this character will never do, so listing them would gate the mission shut forever -- flagged or_branch_unmodelled and left in prose instead. I also did not author a leading rung for 'do your nation's two quests': it would be a target the runtime cannot mark, and with no evidence anywhere in this mission the ladder would sit on it and never draw the door, which costs a marker that is otherwise correct.

notes:
The longest ladder in this lane and the only one with any evidence at all -- three points, and every one of them is obtained AT its own step and absent from the header's Reward field, which is empty.

GIVER -- I DISAGREE WITH BOTH THE HEADER AND CHRONICLE. chronicle_snpc is '' and the header Start says 'Jugner Forest (S)', which is where the PREVIOUS mission left you standing, not where this one asks you to go: bullet 1 sends you to Amaura at Home Point #4 in present-day Southern San d'Oria (G-6). Amaura is the ladder's start, she probes clean, and she is where the marker belongs; the header's zone is kept verbatim in start.raw. Note the era carefully -- Amaura is in Southern San d'Oria (zone 230), the modern city, while Raustigne in the neighbouring missions is in Southern San d'Oria (S) (zone 80). Getting that wrong is a marker on the far side of a time portal.

THE BULB IS TRADED TWICE AND THE PAGE DOES NOT SAY WHETHER IT COMES BACK. Bullet 2 trades a Cernunnos Bulb to Amaura, bullet 3 trades a Cernunnos Bulb to the Humus-rich Earth. Either she returns it or a second one is needed, and the page never says which, so both steps carry one bulb each and the ambiguity is flagged rather than resolved. This is also why the evidence on step 2 is safe in either reading: if she consumes it, holding no bulb correctly drops the mark back to the saplings, and if she returns it the mark stays ahead.

STEP 2 IS THE FARM AND IT IS A REAL RUNG, not a sub-bullet's commentary: bullet 1's sub-bullet says plainly that if you did not farm one after the previous mission you kill Wandering Saplings in Jugner Forest (S) for it. Mobs are marker targets, so this rung draws, and the Cernunnos Bulb is its evidence -- a player who took the previous mission's advice starts already holding one and the ladder skips straight past it to Amaura, who is also step 1's target, so no marker jumps anywhere.

Step 9 is gated on a game-day change AND a zone, neither of which the addon can see (time_gated). The last two rungs are both on Amaura, which is one marker, and only the second carries the Bottle of treant tonic -- the same key item the next mission (A Spoonful of Sugar) is about, so per the brief it is this mission's evidence and that mission's business, never both. Route advice (Home Point #4, the Campaign Arbiter warp, the Norvallen Outpost, the Voidwatch warp), the Lobison aggro warning, the recycled-dialogue aside and the To Cure a Cough collision are all notes, not steps.

THE WALKTHROUGH IS AN IMAGE AND THE IMAGE DID NOT SURVIVE. Bullet 1 reads, in full, 'If strictly interested in mission progression, use the image below for the fastest solution, following the :' -- it ends mid-sentence and the picture it points at is not in the render. Every rung here therefore comes from the After-the-walkthrough section 'Question and Answer - Total of 24 Signatures', whose bullets restart at [1].

WHY THESE FOUR AND NOT THE OTHERS. Farouel, Vichauxdat, Aurfet and Corseihaut answer to 24 signatures between them, and the page's own Rewards List starts its table at '20-29 signatures', so 24 clears whatever the bar is -- that is the spine, and it is the same set the missing image was said to show. The 'Quests' section NPCs (Eumielle, Coucheutand, Hauberliond, Sabiliont, and Rongelouts N Distaud with his rock-paper-scissors game) buy EXTRA signatures with items for a BETTER REWARD -- 30 to 120 signatures walks up an orb/foulard/ingot table -- which is reward optimisation and not progress, so none of them is a rung. Their answers and prices are on the page for anyone who wants them.

NO HAND-IN IS AUTHORED BECAUSE THE PAGE NAMES NONE. Bullet 6 of the Quests section implies a submission prompt ('if you choose to not turn in the current amount of signatures, or deny the confirmation, you will need to zone out and back'), but it names neither an NPC nor a place, and the Description's Vestillet and Noillurie are never given a location. A quest may end without an NPC; inventing one is worse.

ZONE IS INFERRED AND FLAGGED. The page gives a grid for every one of the four and a zone for none of them. The header Start ('Southern San d'Oria (S)') and the Description ('Kingdom troops stationed within the city') put them in the (S) city, which is what every step records -- but it is a reading, not a statement, so all four steps are medium and the record is medium with it. The four are an unordered set, hence the shared group: they draw together, which is also what a player wants when they are all inside one city.

NOTHING HERE IS MARKABLE. There is no NPC, no door, no ??? -- not even a grid; unlike A Timeswept Butterfly, which is also a zone entry but whose Directions section names the Wooden Gate you click, this page names no entity at all and has no After-the-walkthrough section to recover one from. That is the correct outcome, not a defect in the reading: chronicle has no giver for this row either, so nothing is lost and nothing moves. If it is ever to draw, it needs a first-hand observation of what the cutscene trigger is, not a better reading of this page.
